introducing.description: The orange star at the center of the Delta Eridani system. It is cooler than Sol but more than two and a half times as large.

introducing.name: Delta Eridani 4
introducing.description: The fourth inner rocky planet in the Delta Eridani system, also called DE-4. It is slightly larger than Earth, with lower gravity and a somewhat denser atmosphere. Its temperate-to-subtropical landscape mixes meadows, rocky bluffs and forests of huge brownish trees, and its varied wildlife includes six-legged insect and mammal analogues, bird analogues and a colour-changing winged creature Bob calls a hippogriff.
introducing.state: Bob has ruled it out as a colonization target after his concealed drones observed fire-using native inhabitants.

introducing.name: natives
introducing.description: A native population of Delta Eridani 4 that Bob judges to be fire-using and probably intelligent. The beings have bat- and pig-like faces, long spiderish limbs, light brownish-gray to orangey-tan fur, patterned heads, and mobile expressive ears. Bob observes six apparently friendly groups, each tending a fire and interacting with the others.

updates.current_state: At Delta Eridani, establishing mining, communications, and system surveillance before ruling the inhabited fourth planet out as a colonization target.

updates.description: A stellar system centered on an orange star cooler than Sol but more than two and a half times as large. Bob chose it for its lack of a binary companion, low ultraviolet emissions, long-lived stellar type, and wide potential habitable zone; Bill considered it a likely source of habitable planets. Its survey identifies five inner rocky planets and five outer gas giants separated by an asteroid belt. Two outer giants have rings rivaling Saturn's, and the largest is about six Jupiter masses.

A practical drone design for planetary exploration. The football-sized surveillance variant carries cameras, microphones, gripping limbs and small reactors; the meter-long biological-analysis variant has many appendages and mechanical stomachs that analyze local organics in about a day. Both can change color with limited pattern mimicry.

Remote observation and manipulation devices directed through GUPPI. They come in varied sizes, coordinate across scales and, once their tasks are defined, need little supervision. They can inspect ship circuitry with gnat-sized units, carry video cameras and pick up vibrations through a wall. Running on reusable scripts, they feed ore to manufacturing systems, assemble and repair ships, and refine battle scrap into rail-gun ammunition; printers can make more of them. They can explore planetary surfaces, but without infrared, flight or camouflage they do it inefficiently.

summary: Bob establishes mining, communications, and system surveillance before surveying the habitable fourth planet. His concealed drones find a rich forest ecosystem and then evidence of fire-using, communicative natives, leading him to rule the planet out for colonization and to prepare a report for Bill.
